name: Jeiel
overview: Jeiel was a male Levite who held the position of second rank Levite and served as a gatekeeper. His role was significant within the tribe of Levi, which was entrusted with duties related to the worship and service of God. No additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeiel means 'God has preserved' or possibly 'God sweeps up,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's sustaining power. This name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:18 and highlights the divine preservation associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Jeiel is explicitly identified as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the Levitical lineage. Scripture does not record any further family relationships beyond this tribal affiliation.
scriptureSignificance: Jeiel's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his service as a gatekeeper of the second rank among the Levites, a role critical to the orderly worship and protection of the sanctuary. This position underscores the importance of faithful service and dedication to God's house, illustrating the Levites' vital function in Israel's worship life as recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:18.
